# Attribution of the V2 false-positive-rate change

This fixed-seed factorial study separates the legacy generator/detector from the current generator/detector. It uses Seed A 31001 for calibration and Seed B 31002 for evaluation in every cell. It measures synthetic scenario recovery, not real-world fraud performance.

## Conclusion

The FPR decrease from 16.65% to 2.22% is caused by the A-selected threshold moving from 2.5% to 5.0%. At a fixed threshold, legacy and current detector SQL produce the same decision metrics; ranking cannot affect FPR because it orders only already-prioritised cases. The new generator stock mechanics do not change FPR at either fixed threshold, but at 5.0% they raise recall from 65.81% to 82.74% and evasive recall from 6.95% to 57.24%. This is a planted-mechanic benefit, not evidence of real-world generalisation.

The current detector therefore has a more selective operating point, with a material cost: evasive recall remains only 57.24% on V2-B and 49.14% on V2-C. Those misses remain a headline limitation.
